strategies.overview: Ditto sets itself apart from other revenge killers by using Imposter, which makes it an especially flexible Choice Scarf user for picking off setup sweepers like Oricorio-F, Beartic, and Trailblaze Hisuian Sneasel. Ditto's ability to outright deter setup sweepers is tough to replicate for other revenge killers that only work in more specific matchups. For example, Basculin is excellent at finishing off Oricorio-F and Minior, but it can struggle against Beartic in snow as well as Virizion. Ditto's ability to threaten to reverse sweep can even make it a great wincon in its own right. However, Imposter is thwarted by Substitute, and setup sweepers like Mesprit, Minior, and Hisuian Sneasel commonly fit the move. Some setup sweepers, such as Jolteon and Snorlax, can even utilize their defensive boosts and higher HP stats to keep setting up in front of Ditto and wear it down with their attacks. Despite Ditto being generally useful as a revenge killer, it's often overshadowed by more independently powerful and versatile fast attackers like Jolteon, Sneasel, and Choice Scarf Basculin.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Ditto's Tera type is the only flexible thing about it. Tera Fairy is an option over Tera Steel for a different defensive profile. A Fighting resistance is handy against Hitmontop's Mach Punch, Beartic's Close Combat, and Regirock's Body Press, and a Dragon immunity can help Ditto switch into and phaze Dipplin more easily. Tera Ghost is another alternative, one that pushes the Fighting resistance from Tera Fairy even further into an immunity.

Checks and Counters

Substitute Users: Mesprit, Hisuian Sneasel, and other Substitute users can deny Ditto's ability to copy them using Imposter, though they must set up with Substitute before Ditto copies them.

Item Removal: If Ditto loses its Choice Scarf to Knock Off or Trick, it loses most of its reliability as a revenge killer and utility option for deterring setup.

Residual Damage and Status: Relying on Choice Scarf means that Ditto will get worn down by repeatedly taking entry hazard damage, as it will hardly have easy opportunities to heal even if it copies recovery moves. Status also sticks around on Ditto, and paralysis nullifies most of Ditto's potential as a revenge killer.

Trick Room Users: Ditto is helpless to prevent offensive Trick Room users like Spiritomb and Alolan Exeggutor from sweeping past it due to it moving second under Trick Room.

movesets.name: Revenge Killer
movesets.description:
Ditto's sole access to Imposter puts it in a class of its own as an adaptable Choice Scarf revenge killer against a wide range of setup sweepers in ZU, boasting a non-exhaustive list that includes threats like Oricorio-F, Beartic, Minior, Lycanroc, Hisuian Sneasel, Farigiraf, Charizard, and more. The EV spread is for the rare occurence where Ditto is in a mirror matchup, pushing it to activate the opposing Ditto's Imposter first to proceed to PP stall. Tera Steel gives Ditto a good blanket defensive typing and helpful resistances against setup sweepers like Oricorio-P, Mesprit, and Farigiraf. The Rock resistance of Tera Steel is handy for dampening damage from Stealth Rock, Lycanroc's Accelerock, and Minior's Stone Edge.

Bulkier teams appreciate Ditto's flexibility for blanket checking and deterring volatile setup sweepers like Charizard, Beartic, and Oricorio-F. As Ditto can reverse sweep with stolen stat boosts, it acts as a unique wincon option for stall teams, which can often be so passive as to enable many sweepers to get set up. These more defensive teams, including balance teams, can also have bulky teammates like Lanturn, Snorlax, and Regirock waiting in the wings to pivot in for Ditto once it's locked itself into one of its moves. As Ditto is so dependent on its item to function in its role, it relies heavily on Pokemon that can't have their items removed, namely Dipplin and Muk. Knock Off absorbers like Weezing can similarly cover this flaw for Ditto. Since Ditto won't be dealing with Substitute setup sweepers like Mesprit and Mismagius, it appreciates being able to fall back on Haze users and phazers like Weezing and Articuno as well as Prankster Encore users like Sableye and Whimsicott. Ditto suffers against entry hazard stacking teams, notably Toxic Spikes and Sticky Web, so it appreciates teammates like Hitmontop and Sandslash that can remove hazards.

strategies.overview: Ditto is a niche yet potent revenge killer, leveraging its Imposter ability to quickly reverse sweeps, which would otherwise pose a significant threat to its team. Choice Scarf is both Ditto's biggest strength and Achilles' heel, allowing it to outspeed the Pokemon it copies; however, it is limited to choosing one move, allowing its opponent to respond accordingly by switching to a check. Partially due to being Choice-locked, Ditto struggles against opposing defensive Terastallization, where foes may gain a resistance or immunity to Ditto's moves and fire back with a powerful attack. However, due to Ditto’s lack of any defensive utility and being somewhat situational as well as matchup dependent, Ditto is not a common Pokemon.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Due to Ditto being incredibly one-dimensional and lacking almost any versatility, it mostly lacks other options. However, Ditto can choose to run Tera Steel. Tera Steel acts as a midground between Tera Fairy and Tera Ghost, giving Ditto a resistance to Dragon-type moves, a Toxic and Toxic Spikes immunity, and maintaining a resistance to Arceus's Extreme Speed. However, due to Ditto's poor bulk, a resistance might not be enough to keep Ditto alive against powerful attackers such as Koraidon and Miraidon.

Checks and Counters

Protect Users: Protect users like Gliscor take advantage of Ditto being Choice-locked to scout and respond accordingly.

Entry Hazards: Entry hazards significantly cripple Ditto due to its inability to run Heavy-Duty Boots, slowly wearing them down every time it switches in.

movesets.name: Revenge Killer
movesets.description:
Tera Ghost grants Ditto an immunity to Arceus's Extreme Speed and Koraidon's Low Kick, while Tera Normal gives Ditto an immunity to Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage while adding a STAB boost when copying Arceus's Extreme Speed. On the other hand, Tera Fairy gives Ditto immunity to moves such as Koraidon's Outrage and Scale Shot and Miraidon's Draco Meteor. 0 Speed IVs and a Relaxed nature ensure Ditto has the best chance against other Ditto, making Struggle move last and therefore causing recoil the latest, and 248 HP EVs ensure that Ditto gets five uses of Struggle and minimizes entry hazard damage.

Ditto mainly fits on bulkier balance teams, where being passive is less of an issue due to its great revenge killing and reverse sweeping abilities. Furthermore, on more defensive teams, Ditto’s lack of defensive utility is supplemented by other teammates, while it can also more easily rely on teammates to scout for an opponent Terastallizing. More passive teammates like Eternatus, Gliscor, and Alomomola enjoy having extra insurance against powerful threats like Zacian-C or Scale Shot Koraidon. Due to Ditto being Choice locked, defensive Pokemon such as Ho-Oh can take great advantage of Ditto being locked into an unfavorable move. Therefore, Ditto appreciates the support of Eternatus, which provides a Toxic poison immunity and a strong STAB attack in Dynamax Cannon in combination with Toxic, which can quickly wear Ho-Oh down. Ditto also appreciates teammates like Alomomola, which can help Ditto that are Choice-locked into Dragon- or Ghost-type moves and safely switch out against Pokemon like Zacian-C and Arceus.

strategies.outdated: These analyses were written before Pokemon Home's update for Generation 9. As a result, some of the content may now be outdated as we adjust for the new metagame.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
• Ditto is a niche revenge killer that can also be used to attempt a reverse sweep, but it must be wary of threats that may counter it with a surprise Terastallization, such as Tera Fairy Miraidon, Tera Fire Koraidon, Tera Ice Iron Bundle, and Tera Water Gholdengo.
  • Ditto doesn't add much value to teams on its own outside of helping overwhelm opposing checks. It is also strongly prediction reliant.
  • Maximum bulk and minimum Speed allow Ditto to force opposing Ditto to trigger Imposter first and run out of PP quicker.
  • Tera Fairy defeats Choice Scarf Miraidon, Koraidon, and Walking Wake that may try to attack it with a Dragon-type move.
  • Ditto is rarely a reliable check for reasons explained earlier, so it appreciates support from backup checks, especially for potent threats that it fails to revenge kill such as Swords Dance Chien-Pao, Double Dance Miraidon, and Bulk Up Great Tusk. Thus, teammates like Toxapex, Skeledirge, Ting-Lu, Clodsire, and Iron Treads are good picks.
  • Ditto's ability to revenge kill many strong threats makes teambuilding flexible, allowing offensive Pokemon like Miraidon, Iron Bundle, Chien-Pao, and Koraidon to fit more easily.

movesets.name: Imposter
movesets.description: Ditto is a great revenge killer that fits mainly on stall and balance teams for its ability to punish and discourage opposing setup sweepers; however, Ditto's strengths allow it to be useful to any teamstyle. Ditto runs 248 HP to minimize Stealth Rock damage and allow it to use Struggle up to five times from full HP. A Quiet nature and 252 Special Attack EVs allow Ditto to maximize Future Sight Damage when transformed into Pokemon like Slowbro and Reuniclus, as Future Sight damage is based on Ditto's Special Attack before transforming. A Choice Scarf lets Ditto outrun the Pokemon that it is transforming into without having to rely on a Speed tie. Tera Steel reduces Stealth Rock damage and is a good defensive Tera type, helping out specifically when transformed into Gardevoir and Hisuian Goodra. Ditto pairs well with defensive Pokemon such as Hippowdon and Hisuian Goodra, which can take hits directed at Ditto after it revenge kills or forces out the opposing Pokemon. Ditto also pairs well with passive Pokemon such as Empoleon, Chansey, and Chesnaught that may get set up on, which can allow Ditto to come in and revenge kill those setup sweepers. Ditto also benefits from strong entry hazard control from Pokemon like Cyclizar and Talonflame, which allows it to come in multiple times over the course of the game. Ditto has trouble when transforming into opposing Choice Scarf Pokemon such as Mienshao, Gengar, and Gardevoir, due to having to rely on winning a Speed tie. Similarly, Ditto has trouble with Pokemon running Substitute like Suicune.

strategies.comments:
Other Options

Ditto can use other Tera types to help itself against particular targets. Tera Dark provides an immunity to Psyshock to turn the tables on Calm Mind Meloetta and Galarian Slowbro.

Checks and Counters

Unburden Sweepers: Grafaiai and Hitmonlee won't have their Unburden boost copied by Imposter.

Substitute Users: Sweepers like Raikou, Uxie, and Meloetta can protect themselves from Ditto's Imposter with Substitute.

Item Removal: Without Choice Scarf, Ditto is not as effective of a revenge killer. However, Ditto can absorb Knock Off to improve its matchup against stall teams that depend on Regenerator users.

Residual Damage: Ditto's bad HP sticks with it even after it copies its target, and its role as a Choice Scarf user limits its longevity against anything but Regenerator users.

movesets.name: Among Us (Imposter)
movesets.description:
Set Details

Ditto distinguishes itself with the entirely unique combination of Imposter + Choice Scarf. Ditto's ability enables it to morph into a revenge killer with great potential to reverse sweep teams with the boosts it copies, so it deters setup sweepers like Flygon, Cinccino, Munkidori, Paldean Tauros-W, Toxtricity, and Scyther. Maximum physical bulk and minimum Speed help Ditto to trigger an opposing Ditto's Imposter first and PP stall it. Tera Steel helps Ditto against Cinccino, Flygon, Alolan Ninetales, and Oricorio-P, and it can turn the tables for Ditto in risky Speed ties against Choice Scarf variants of Flamigo and Porygon-Z. Lessened damage from Stealth Rock and a Toxic Spikes immunity are also nice perks from Tera Steel. Tera Fairy provides Ditto a neat defensive typing with helpful Dark, Bug, and Fighting resistances to better stomach priority moves like Sucker Punch, First Impression, Mach Punch, and Vacuum Wave. The Normal and Fighting immunities from Tera Ghost help Ditto against Cincinno and Porygon-Z, Paldean Tauros-W and other Fighting-types, and bulky Body Press sweepers like Bronzong.

Ditto is a good filler option for teams in need of an emergency answer to setup sweepers, and most teams can appreciate Ditto's ability to check weather teams by copying Speed-boosting weather abilities like Swift Swim, Slush Rush, and Chlorophyll. Stall teams can rely on Ditto as an anti-setup option that provides opportunities they'd otherwise lack for reverse sweeping. Offensive teams can worry less about fitting defensive counterplay for major offensive threats by running Ditto, and Ditto itself can work as a wincon if it copies a setup sweeper. Balance teams appreciate Ditto's ability to deter offensive setup sweepers, and they have the defensive backbone necessary to compensate for Ditto needing to switch out after being locked into a move by Choice Scarf. The virtually infinite PP Ditto can bring with Imposter helps in matchups against stall teams, and it can use Imposter to copy abilities like Regenerator from Amoonguss and Natural Cure from Altaria. Imposter's ability to overwrite the Speed drop from Sticky Web and copy Speed-boosting weather abilities helps Ditto out against hyper offense teams, lessening the strain Cinccino and other fast threats like Choice Scarf Flygon are under to answer these teams. However, Ditto itself can be surprised by Terastallization from threats like Flygon and Scyther, so it relies on secondary checks to setup sweepers. Scream Tail can disrupt setup sweepers with its fast Encore, while Ditto exploits threats that continue to try and boost against it, such as Oricorio-P.

movesets.name: Revenge Killer
movesets.description:
Ditto finds a small but notable niche as a unique, if a bit unreliable, revenge killer and reverse sweeper thanks to Imposter. The specific EV spread makes Ditto as bulky as possible while also minimizing entry hazard damage as much as possible. 0 Speed IVs and a Sassy nature allow Ditto to have the best odds possible winning the mirror matchup. Choice Scarf allows Ditto to be a consistent revenge killer once transformed. Ditto does not often Terastallize, but Tera Steel gives a great defensive typing against sweepers like Florges and Bruxish while providing an immunity to Toxic. Tera Ghost alternatively allows Ditto to block Extreme Speed and Fake Out from Arcanine and Ambipom, respectively. Finally, Tera Fairy gives a resistance to Sucker Punch from Pokemon like Skuntank and Zoroark while allowing Ditto to, in a pinch, check Pokemon like Hariyama and Tatsugiri.

Ditto generally is used on more specialized bulkier balance teams that need its support to deal with setup sweepers. Ditto can't lose its Choice Scarf without it being effectively neutered, so Knock Off absorbers such as Mudsdale and Hisuian Decidueye are great teammates to have. Ditto also can't deal with Substitute-using setup sweepers such as Salazzle, Paldean Tauros-F, and Hisuian Typhlosion, so checks to these threats such as Rhydon and Milotic are imperative. Ditto cannot be a consistent revenge killer against other Choice Scarf users like Hisuian Decidueye and Bruxish and Pokemon such as Florges and Hisuian Qwilfish can check them. In the same vein, Knock Off users such as Skuntank, Zoroark, and Pawmot are useful to have because they wear walls like Rhydon, Hisuian Qwilfish, and Alolan Sandslash down for a transformed Ditto to break through.

strategies.outdated: This analysis was uploaded prior to The Indigo Disk release and may contain outdated information.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf Revenge Killer
movesets.description:
Thanks to Ditto's signature ability Imposter, which also copies enemy stat changes, Ditto is one of the best revenge killers in the tier. Ditto's presence alone scares off sweepers like Ogerpon-W and Azumarill from setting up. Ditto does not copy the enemy HP stat, so 248 HP EVs are used to minimize damage taken from entry hazards before transforming while maximizing Ditto's HP stat, as well as allowing Ditto to use Struggle four times before it faints. 252 Defense EVs minimize the damage Ditto takes from opposing Ditto in the extremely rare mirror matchup. Finally, a Relaxed nature coupled with 0 Speed IVs guarantees that Imposter will never activate first, which ensures that Ditto will have more Transform PP in the aforementioned mirror match.

Ursaluna is a great teammate for Ditto, as it can switch into walls and begin applying immediate pressure. Ditto also appreciates Ursaluna's unrivaled ability to punch holes in the opposing team, making a late-game Ditto sweep much easier. If Ditto copies certain targets like Iron Valiant and a majority of the opposing team is weakened, Ditto can win the game. Terapagos removes entry hazards, is a one-time check against threats such as Latios, Urshifu-R, and Sneasler, and beats bulky setup sweepers such as Swords Dance Gliscor that Ditto struggles with despite copying their boosts. Porygon-2 is a defensive wall that goads opposing types such as Dragon, Dark, and Fire to setup its threats to break through Porygon-2, allowing Ditto to come in and clean up these types by copying a boosted Dragonite, Darkrai, or Ceruledge late-game. Indeedee is a good teammate for Ditto, as its Psychic Surge ability prevents Ditto from being picked off by priority moves. Blissey is a nice partner for Ditto, as it can absorb status moves that would otherwise cripple Ditto and then shrug them off via Natural Cure. Blissey can also use Thunder Wave to slow down opposing Choice Scarf users that would otherwise Speed tie with Ditto such as Meowscarada and Enamorus. Choice Specs Hisuian Zoroark is a powerful teammate that pairs well with Ditto, as Ditto can copy the stat boosts from setup sweepers that aim to take advantage of a Choice-locked Hisuian Zoroark. Maushold can use its high speed tier to lock Bulk Up users like Landorus-T that would otherwise be able to stall out Ditto. Additionally, Maushold is able to break down walls due to the sheer power of Population Bomb. Pivots are great teammates for Ditto because they can lure in targets for Ditto to copy. Choice Scarf Staraptor and Defensive Braviary are solid picks, as they can use U-turn to go right into Ditto. Braviary is also capable of using Defog to keep Ditto alive for longer.

strategies.outdated: This analysis was for Battle Stadium Singles Regulation C, which ended on June 30th, 2023. Since then, this Pokemon's viability has massively dropped off, and it is no longer relevant. Using this Pokemon in today's metagame is not advised unless you have an extremely niche, hyper-specific need to cover.

movesets.name: Revenge Killer
movesets.description:
• Ditto is widely hailed as the best revenge killer and finds a small niche with a Choice Scarf.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Ditto rarely needs to Terastallize unless it is being threatened by Dragon Dance Dragonite's Extreme Speed at +3.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost gives Ditto immunity to Dragonite's Extreme Speed, preventing it from defeating Ditto after three Dragon Dances.

Items
  • Choice Scarf: The safest option, Choice Scarf guarantees that Ditto will always outspeed the foe unless said foe is holding a Choice Scarf.
  • Focus Sash: A high-risk yet high-reward option, Focus Sash allows Ditto to switch moves at the cost of being nullified by entry hazards. However, it should be noted that Imposter doesn't copy Protosynthesis or Quark Drive boosts, making Focus Sash a lot less niche, as it allows Ditto to beat foes such as Flutter Mane more consistently assuming the field is clear of hazards.
EV Spreads
  • Effort Values: The given EVs maximize Ditto's bulk in the rare case of a mirror matchup.
  • Individual Values: 0 Speed IVs and a minus Speed nature is key to beating opposing Ditto, as the Ditto that moves last on the fourth turn will win the mirror.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
Ditto is used for its phenomenal ability to transform into strong opposing Pokemon, which is invaluable in a format with Restricted Pokemon, giving you access to an extra extremely powerful Pokemon. Ditto is a good late-game cleaner that likes copying Pokemon such as Calyrex-S and Miraidon, since it outspeeds and threatens an OHKO onto both of them. Choice Scarf is used to allow Ditto to outspeed the Pokemon it transforms into, giving Ditto the advantage while fighting it. Tera Ghost is used to give Ditto an immunity to Fake Out, which can severely hinder its momentum.

Terapagos can be an issue for Ditto, since if Terapagos Terastallizes, Imposter will not work, and Terapagos will OHKO it. Ditto also struggles with Pokemon that can slow its momentum, such as Rillaboom and Incineroar with the aforementioned Fake Out and Amoonguss with Spore and Rage Powder. Fighting-types, such as Iron Hands and the Urshifu formes, can help against Incineroar and Terapagos, and Ice-types, such as Chien-Pao and Calyrex-I, can help against Amoonguss and Rillaboom. Incineroar and Amoonguss are also good partners for Ditto, as they help it get attacks off with Spore, Rage Powder, and Fake Out support. The aforementioned Urshifu-R, Iron Hands, and Incineroar can help Ditto position itself and transform into the ideal foe with U-Turn, Volt Switch, and Parting Shot respectively.

movesets.name: Focus Sash
movesets.description:
Set Details

  • Ditto is uniquely able to punish teams using Restricted Pokemon that threaten opposing species of themselves, and it often serves as a third Restricted Pokemon. Common threats such as Calyrex-S, Zamazenta-C, Miraidon, and Lunala all use STAB moves that hit themselves for super effective damage, making Ditto extremely effective against them.
  • Additionally, Ditto can copy the boosts that Calyrex-S and Zamazenta-C get from their respective abilities, deterring a full sweep or even setup in the case of Nasty Plot Calyrex-S. In particular, since Zamazenta-C gets a Defense boost from Dauntless Shield, Ditto copies that boost then activates its own Dauntless Shield, allowing it to hit Zamazenta-C harder.
  • Ditto can have unique case-by-case applications when transforming into support Pokemon such as Incineroar and Amoonguss, but Ditto is often best used to copy the opponent's Restricted Pokemon.
  • Focus Sash guarantees that Ditto survives an attack if it loses the Speed tie with whatever it has transformed into, ensuring that Ditto can operate around the mandatory Speed tie while maintaining the flexibility to use other moves the foe grants it, unlike Choice Scarf. Focus Sash also helps Ditto work around its low HP, transforming into frailer Pokemon, and has general defensive utility against the powerful attacks of Regulation I.
  • Tera Ghost is generally useful to keep Ditto's Focus Sash intact against Fake Out and helps immensely against Zamazenta-C, allowing it to avoid Body Press altogether if Ditto copies it. Tera Ghost can also provide a boost to Astral Barrage if Ditto copies Calyrex-S.

Teambuilding

  • Being mindful of which slots Ditto can come in on and switching accordingly is key, as Imposter will transform Ditto into the Pokemon directly across from it. Forcing Ditto to copy a disadvantageous, usually support-oriented, Pokemon is a great way for opponents to deal with the threat.
  • Maintaining Focus Sash can be important to work around Ditto's low HP stat. Priority moves such as Fake Out, Thunderclap from Raging Bolt, and Sucker Punch from Chien-Pao are especially threatening for Ditto, since these moves will either threaten to break its Focus Sash or pick it off outright.
  • Pokemon that resist their STAB moves, such as Landorus and Calyrex-I, can hamper Ditto's effectiveness when transforming into them. Rillaboom in particular can tank its own moves, set Grassy Terrain to hamper a potential Miraidon partner, and can threaten to break Ditto's Focus Sash with both Fake Out and Grassy Glide.
  • Urshifu-R can cut through Focus Sash with Surging Strikes, depending somewhat on what Ditto transformed into, and can pick off a weakened Ditto with Aqua Jet. Choice Scarf Urshifu-R is also an excellent check to Ditto as Calyrex-S, which could otherwise sweep entire teams with stolen boosts.
  • Galarian Weezing turns off Imposter completely, which effectively forces Ditto out of the match. Toxic Spikes and Poison Gas can also easily break its Focus Sash and bring it into KO range, especially if it is forced to remain as Ditto.
  • Ditto cannot transform into Terastallized Terapagos and Ogerpon-H. This uniquely helps Terapagos and Ogerpon-H leverage their boosts against Ditto teams that would otherwise try to turn them against themselves.
  • Thunder Wave Grimmsnarl is a standout speed control Pokemon that can help Ditto avoid Speed ties, which are important in the cases of Calyrex-S and Zamazenta-C. It can also apply Reflect and Light Screen to help transformed Ditto survive attacks from Restricted Pokemon, which is especially helpful given its low HP.
  • Incineroar and Miraidon can help pivot Ditto into advantageous transformations with U-turn or Parting Shot and Volt Switch, respectively.
  • Calyrex-I particularly has a hard time against Calyrex-S and Zamazenta-C, especially if they are paired together, so it appreciates Ditto being able to check one or both of them. Calyrex-I also threatens Rillaboom and Landorus, which Ditto struggles against.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 8

Price Range: 3-4 points

Overview: Ditto’s viability in a matchup completely depends on the opponent’s Pokemon and movesets, making it odd and unique. It can scout opposing Pokemon by transforming into them while also functioning as a nearly catch-all revenge killer that can even revenge kill boosted opposing Pokemon. Its presence in a matchup also makes setup-reliant Pokemon think twice. However, Ditto’s lack of reliability due to being able to specifically prepare for it in a draft setting, dearth of defensive utility, and relative lack of value compared to other low tiers leave much to be desired.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Revenge Killer: Using a Choice Scarf, Ditto is able to scout the opposing Pokemon and then outspeed and revenge kill it, even if it has a Speed boost, keeping otherwise dangerous setup sweepers in check.

Common Items

Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf allows Ditto to outspeed non-Choice Scarf opposing Pokemon, letting it move first and revenge kill them. This is far and away its best and most consistent item.

Niche Items

Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots allows Ditto to function better as a scout and pivot when facing bulkier teams, as it becomes immune to entry hazard damage and can switch in and out repeatedly.

Tera

It is not recommended to make Ditto a Tera Captain due to its inconsistent nature. If one does choose Ditto as a Tera Captain, generally good defensive Tera types such as Tera Fairy, Steel, and Water could help in a pinch. Specific Tera types that allow it to handily win a 1v1 can also be used, such as Tera Poison for Iron Valiant or coverage types to counter anticipated foes with advantageous Tera Blast coverage. Do NOT use Tera Stellar on Ditto, as it makes Imposter and Transform fail.

Draft Strategy

Ditto is very flexible due to its unique profile, and it can therefore theoretically fit on any team. However, it must be noted that outside of scouting and revenge killing, it offers little to no utility nor defensive integrity to a team, making it hard to fit. Ditto is a complementary piece to an otherwise complete team, so it is recommended for teams to pack as much utility and defensive integrity in as little team slots as possible before considering it.

Intricacies of the Imposter

Ditto’s Imposter is a mechanically complex ability and has a lot of niche interactions. The most noteworthy interactions are written below. Knowledge of such interactions and using the appropriate optimizations would make the most value out of one’s Ditto.

Ditto Mirror: In a Ditto mirror match, maximum bulk and minimum Speed allow Ditto to force opposing Ditto to trigger Imposter first and run out of PP quicker. It is therefore recommended to run max Defense, a Relaxed nature, and 0 Speed IVs.

Future Sight: If Ditto uses Future Sight while transformed and is not on the field when the Future Sight hits the foe, its base Special Attack stat is used for damage calculation. Therefore, in matchups where Future Sight is a possibility, such as against Galarian Slowking, it is recommended to max out Ditto’s Special Attack.

Terastallization: A Terastallized Ditto maintains the regular properties of a Terastallized Pokemon. If it copies a Terastallized Pokemon, its Tera type and therefore Tera Blast typing are not copied. A Terastallized Ditto’s typing does not change to its transformed target, and it instead keeps its Tera type. If it Terastallizes into the Stellar-type, Imposter and Transform will both fail.

Tera Type-locked Pokemon: Ditto cannot Terastallize against the base formes of Ogerpon and Terapagos regardless of Tera type. It also cannot transform into the Terastallized Ogerpon formes and Terapagos-S. Therefore, it is not recommended to use Ditto as a countermeasure to these Pokemon.

Checks and Counters

Imposter Counters: A Ditto without Imposter is merely fodder. It notably cannot transform into terastallized formes of Ogerpon, making it unable to revenge kill them. Abilities that disable Imposter, such as Neutralizing Gas, render it completely useless. Abilities that it cannot copy the effects of, most notably the Speed boost from Unburden, Protosynthesis, and Quark Drive, may also prove problematic. When able to specifically prepare for Ditto, opponents can limit its effectiveness in several ways. The most common way of doing so is Substitute, which blocks Imposter. Other methods such as using moves that are completely walled by another teammate, or using Terastallization; either using Tera Blast, which Ditto cannot copy, as the Pokemon’s main damage output, or using Tera to improve the defensive matchup or outright wall it; are all valid strategies to prevent it from revenge killing foes.

Defense Boosting: Defense boosting makes Ditto unable to break through the setup Pokemon it is tasked to revenge kill in the limited 5 PP that it has after transforming. Pokemon such as Bulk Up Palafin, Bulk Up Annihilape, and Calm Mind Terapagos cannot be easily revenge killed by Ditto.

Entry Hazards: As Ditto usually does not carry Heavy-Duty Boots and likes to switch in and out to reset its Imposter, entry hazards dig into its longevity and limits its ability to scout and revenge kill opposing Pokemon.

movesets.name: Scarf Imposter
movesets.description: Ditto solidifies itself to once again be the goo that holds balanced and offensive Normal teams together thanks to its incredibly strong ability in Imposter. Reversing the momentum of fast offensive threats such as Iron Valiant, Mega Charizard X, and Excadrill allows Ditto to force counterplay against offensive teams. Ditto can also take advantage of entry hazard setters and removers, such as Ferrothorn, Kleavor, and Zapdos, using their own longevity or utility against them. In order to take advantage of Pokemon that use either Return or Frustration, such as Mega Altaria or Mega Pinsir, Ditto likes to run 128 Happiness instead of 255 or 0. Walls like Blissey and Porygon2 appreciate Ditto being able to prevent threats such as Baxcalibur and Spectrier from using them as setup fodder, while Ditto appreciates both defensive switch-ins and slow pivots via their use of Teleport. Mega Lopunny is a staple on Normal teams that accents Ditto's role expertly; many of the offensive threats and setup sweepers that revenge kill Mega Lopunny, such as Mega Charizard X, Kommo-o, and Galarian Moltres, are usually very weak to their own sets or coverage. Mega Lopunny can lure a threat in and pivot with U-turn, allowing Ditto to come in safely and transform. Ditto appreciates Mega Lopunny's Speed tier and fast pivot with U-turn, as well as potentially setting up Ditto with Encore Sets to stop foes from using Substitute or setting up completely. Hisuian Zoroark makes for another stellar teammate for Ditto, as Hisuian Zoroark disguised as a passive Pokemon, such as Blissey, or another offensive threat, such as Diggersby or Mega Lopunny, can lead to Hisuian Zoroark wallbreaking and netting KOs on vital foes, making it easier for Ditto to sweep once it has transformed. While Ditto is immune to Sticky Web, it is susceptible to other hazards such as Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes, so forms of hazard control such as Staraptor or Cyclizar are appreciated. Staraptor is another defensive option, while Cyclizar can enable Ditto to utilize Transform with a Substitute from Shed Tail. Smeargle on more offense-oriented teams' pairs well with Ditto, as Smeargle can set hazards with Stone Axe or Ceaseless Edge and spread status with Nuzzle, Mortal Spin, or Spore, allowing Ditto to exploit the opposing team easier. Smeargle will usually give up Sticky Web when paired with Ditto so as to not hinder Ditto's revenge killing prowess.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
• Choice Scarf Ditto fills a role as a revenge killer with a chance to reverse sweep entire teams. Its presence discourages setup from foes such as Zacian-C, Mega Salamence, and Primal Groudon. Its ability to generate endless PP also helps against stall teams.
  • In the rare case there is a Ditto mirror, the EVs, IVs, and nature maximize the chance that the opposing Ditto’s Imposter ability activates first, thus causing it to run out of PP first.
  • Tera Ghost allows Ditto to block Extreme Speed from Arceus, since it cannot OHKO Arceus with Extreme Speed or Tera Ghost Arceus with Shadow Claw at +2 from full, while Arceus can at the expense of Tera Normal thanks to Ditto’s low HP stat.
  • Tera Fairy provides a resistance to Sucker Punch and Foul Play, making it harder for Yveltal and Arceus-Dark to revenge kill Ditto. Tera Fairy also provides a useful immunity to Dragon-type moves, letting Ditto soft check Eternatus and Palkia-O.
  • Tera Dark also resists Sucker Punch and Foul Play while also providing a resistance to Marshadow’s Shadow Sneak. Thanks to Tera Dark’s immunity to Psychic, it allows Ditto to absorb powerful attacks such as +1 Light that Burns the Sky from Ultra Necrozma and Psycho Boost from Deoxys-A.
  • Hidden Power Ice allows Ditto to hit Zygarde and Mega Salamence with a super effective move in the rare case Ditto copies a Marshadow with Hidden Power.
  • Ditto should be swapped in carefully, as any unnecessary damage can compromise its role. Due to its low HP stat, Ditto struggles defensively even when transforming into walls such as Chansey.
  • Ditto greatly helps in the hyper offense matchup by restricting the opponent from setting up in addition to Imposter taking away Sticky Web's Speed drop, keeping teammates such as Eternatus, Ho-Oh and Yveltal from being overwhelmed by boosting threats such as Primal Groudon, Zacian-C, and Ultra Necrozma.
  • Ditto can be used to greatly help in the stall matchup thanks to its ability to generate endless PP. Ditto stays healthy by copying recovery moves from Chansey, Dondozo, and Arceus-Dark. Ditto also increases its longevity by copying abilities such as Natural Cure from Chansey and Regenerator from Ho-Oh, and Alomomola.
  • Ditto is a good fit on balance teams, as it helps Defoggers such as Ho-Oh and Yveltal from being overwhelmed by hyper offense threats such as Primal Groudon and Ultra Necrozma. In return, Ho-Oh and Yveltal keep entry hazards off the field, since Ditto can easily get worn down by them.
  • Teammates such as Primal Groudon and Zygarde are free to use more offensive sets thanks to Ditto being able to check threats such as Zacian-C, Eternatus, and opposing Primal Groudon for them. In addition, Zygarde appreciates Ditto allowing it to run a specially defensive set for Arceus-Water instead.
  • Due to being locked into one move, Ditto can be countered by a surprise Tera from threats such as Tera Fairy Eternatus and Tera Ghost Arceus, so another form of reliable revenge killing such as Arceus and Choice Band Marshadow is appreciated.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
248 HP EVs ensure that Ditto will be able to use Struggle four times before fainting, and 252 Defense EVs minimize Struggle damage from an opposing Ditto. The minimum possible Speed allows Imposter to not activate first and therefore allow Ditto to have more Transform PP.

This is a sample set, stay tuned for future updates!
